title: Generalise the 3.7 interaction model and transaction specification
requirements:
- Use provider/consumer for service direction; reserve initiator/responder for transaction patterns
- Define what a 'fully specified' transaction contains
- State that each supported access channel (UI, API) must meet applicable requirements
- Show how event-driven, asynchronous, batch and user-initiated interactions are modelled, with a second figure example
- Introduce maturity states for interactions and restrict formal conformance claims to testable ones
- Require consistent enforcement of business rules, consent, security and audit across channels
- Clarify how human actors, devices and external services participate in interactions
- Identify the 'other means' for specifying non-IHE or human-initiated interactions
